question.text: For a bond selling at a discount, which of the following relationships between Coupon Rate (CR), Current Yield (CY), and Yield to Maturity (YTM) holds true?

answer.text: Coupon rate is greater than current yield, and current yield is greater than YTM
Coupon rate, current yield, and YTM are all equal
Coupon rate is lower than current yield, and current yield is lower than YTM
YTM is lower than coupon rate, and coupon rate is lower than current yield

explanation.text: The Logic: When a bond sells at a discount, its market price is below face value. Current yield = annual coupon divided by market price, so a lower market price pushes current yield above the coupon rate. YTM is higher still because it also captures the capital gain from the price rising to par at maturity. The resulting ordering is: coupon rate is lower than current yield, and current yield is lower than YTM. The Trap: The reverse ordering — coupon rate greater than current yield, greater than YTM — applies to premium bonds, not discount bonds. Candidates often flip the direction. Note: The explanation was rewritten to spell out the comparisons in words ("lower than" / "greater than") instead of raw comparison symbols, because the previous version was being truncated where the symbols had been swallowed. The unsupported Cross-Exam Context and Pro-Tip paragraphs were removed.
